entries.canonical_name: Calculate Audit Sample Size

requires_semantics: Confidence level and tolerable error rate

entries.business_meaning: Computes the minimum sample size needed for statistical audit testing given specified confidence and error tolerance.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Correct application of statistical formula for sample size determination in audit context.
assembly_hints: Combine with population data to select sample
Use for any audit sampling task

entries.canonical_name: Compute Quarter-on-Quarter Variance

requires_semantics: Two quarter data columns (Q2 and Q3 values)

entries.business_meaning: Calculates the percentage or absolute variance between two consecutive quarters for audit analysis.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Correct handling of zero or negative base values.
assembly_hints: Can be applied to any period-over-period comparison
Often combined with sample selection

entries.canonical_name: Select Audit Sample with Criteria Coverage

provides_semantics: Selected sample rows marked with indicator
Coverage of all criteria across selected samples

entries.business_meaning: Selects a subset of rows from a population for audit testing such that each sample satisfies at least one criterion and all criteria are covered collectively.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Ensuring coverage of all criteria with minimum sample size, avoiding duplicate coverage, combinatorial optimization.
assembly_hints: Combine with population data
Use sample size from skill 'Calculate Audit Sample Size'

entries.canonical_name: Apply Foreign Tax Withholding to Revenue
entries.business_meaning: Reduces gross revenue by applicable foreign tax withholding rates to compute net revenue, handling multiple countries with different rates.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Correct application of percentage rates per country and ensuring accurate subtraction.
failure_modes: Applying rate to net instead of gross
assembly_hints: Combine with currency conversion skill
Use for international revenue reporting

entries.canonical_name: Convert Foreign Currency to USD for Reporting
entries.business_meaning: Converts monetary values from various currencies to a single reporting currency (USD) for consistent financial reporting.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Handling exchange rate source and date applicability.
assembly_hints: Combine with withholding skill
Use for multinational financial statements

entries.canonical_name: Amortize Prepaid Expenses Over Period

requires_semantics: Invoice details with amounts and period

entries.business_meaning: Spreads the cost of a prepaid expense over its useful life on a monthly basis, tracking original amount, monthly expense, and remaining balance.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Determining amortization period correctly, handling partial months, allocation across multiple invoices.
failure_modes: Mismatch between total and monthly amounts
assembly_hints: Combine with summary reports
Use for any prepaid asset accounting

entries.canonical_name: Summarize Prepaid Account Balances

requires_semantics: Detailed amortization schedules for prepaid expenses and insurance

provides_semantics: Ending balance as of report date

entries.business_meaning: Aggregates totals from detailed prepaid schedules into a high-level summary snapshot for reporting.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Ensuring totals match detailed schedules, correct YTD calculations.
assembly_hints: Combine with amortization schedule skill
Use for month-end close

entries.canonical_name: Reconcile Source Totals to Report Line Items
entries.business_meaning: Verifies that totals from detailed source files match the aggregated amounts in financial report line items, identifying and adjusting discrepancies.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Handling multiple source files with different formats, ensuring all transactions are captured, proper period cut-off.
assembly_hints: Combine with consolidation skill
Use for month-end close process

entries.canonical_name: Consolidate Period Financial Data from Multiple Sources
entries.business_meaning: Combines financial data from disparate source systems (payroll, accruals, general ledger) into a unified financial package for a reporting period.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Ensuring all sources are incorporated correctly, handling different data structures, maintaining data integrity.
assembly_hints: Part of month-end close process
Use reconciliation skill to verify totals

entries.canonical_name: Compute Accrual Entries from Supporting Schedules
entries.business_meaning: Calculates accrual amounts (e.g., bonuses, miscellaneous) based on underlying data and updates the financial package accordingly.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Correctly applying accrual methodology, ensuring consistency with prior periods.
assembly_hints: Combine with consolidation skill
Use for month-end adjustments

entries.canonical_name: Competitive Market Position Assessment
entries.business_meaning: Analyze a company's current market position relative to competitors, identifying strengths, weaknesses, and strategic imperatives.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires synthesizing qualitative and quantitative competitive dynamics without explicit structured data.
assembly_hints: Combine with strategic opportunity assessment to form a complete strategy presentation.

entries.canonical_name: Strategic Opportunity and Imperative Articulation
entries.business_meaning: Translate market analysis into specific, actionable growth strategies and recommendations.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Must balance ambition with realism, considering local regulations, supply constraints, and user experience.
assembly_hints: Follows competitive assessment; can be paired with risk analysis.

entries.canonical_name: Branch or Segment Data Aggregation with Selection
entries.business_meaning: Aggregate financial data by branch or segment, allowing user selection of specific branches or overall company view.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Implementing dynamic dropdown and ensuring aggregation consistency.
assembly_hints: Often combined with income statement and variance analysis.

entries.canonical_name: Compensation Expense Calculation by Category
entries.business_meaning: Calculate total compensation expense broken down by compensation type (e.g., base salary, bonuses) using headcount and rate assumptions.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Multiple compensation types may have different calculation rules (e.g., hourly vs fixed).
assembly_hints: Can be combined with quarterly reporting and scenario analysis.

entries.canonical_name: Quarterly Period Aggregation and Reporting
entries.business_meaning: Aggregate financial data from monthly or periodic data into quarterly summaries.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Ensuring correct period mapping and handling partial quarters.
assembly_hints: Often used for compensation or revenue reporting.

entries.canonical_name: Scenario Analysis with Input Parameter Modeling
entries.business_meaning: Build a model that allows changing input drivers (e.g., rates, terms) to see projected results and growth rates under different scenarios.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Designing flexible input fields and ensuring calculations update correctly; projecting multiple years.
assembly_hints: Used for financial planning and sensitivity analysis.

entries.canonical_name: Capital Investment Evaluation with Directional NPV/IRR
entries.business_meaning: Perform high-level financial analysis of investment projects using net present value and internal rate of return estimates, with qualitative justification.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Dealing with directional estimates rather than exact numbers; balancing quantitative and qualitative factors.
assembly_hints: Follows by risk identification and mitigation.

entries.canonical_name: Financial and Operational Risk Identification
entries.business_meaning: Identify the top financial and operational risks associated with a project or investment.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires domain knowledge to foresee and prioritize risks.
assembly_hints: Often paired with mitigation strategy.

entries.canonical_name: Risk Mitigation Strategy Formulation
entries.business_meaning: Develop specific strategies to mitigate identified risks and suggest contingency plans.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Creating actionable and robust contingency plans.
assembly_hints: Follows risk identification; part of investment recommendation.

entries.canonical_name: Payroll Calculation by Contract Categories
entries.business_meaning: Calculate weekly payroll amounts for each employee based on collective bargaining agreement categories and rates.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Multiple payroll categories with different calculation rules (e.g., per diem, mileage).
assembly_hints: Must include CBA compliance validation and flexible roster.

entries.canonical_name: Collective Bargaining Agreement Compliance Validation
entries.business_meaning: Check payroll inputs against collective bargaining agreement terms to highlight conflicts or violations.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Interpreting CBA rules and applying them to variable inputs; multiple conditions.
assembly_hints: Integrated into payroll model; user inputs trigger validation.

entries.canonical_name: Flexible Roster and Production Schedule Configuration
entries.business_meaning: Design a payroll model that can accommodate any orchestra configuration or production run duration, easily updatable for changing rates.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Building a flexible structure that scales to different ensemble sizes and contract terms.
failure_modes: Model too rigid for new scenarios
assembly_hints: Underpins the payroll calculation and compliance features.

entries.canonical_name: Retrieve and normalize financial data from open web
entries.business_meaning: Ability to fetch publicly available financial data for a given set of companies and organize it into a structured format.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Ensuring data completeness and accuracy from multiple public sources.
assembly_hints: Often combined with data validation and cleaning skills.

entries.canonical_name: Compute LTM and NTM PE multiples
entries.business_meaning: Ability to calculate trailing and forward price-to-earnings multiples from stock price and earnings data.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Handling different fiscal years and analyst consensus estimates.
assembly_hints: Requires synchronized price and earnings data.

entries.canonical_name: Aggregate weighted metrics by hierarchical sector group
entries.business_meaning: Ability to compute weighted averages and percentage contributions for sub-groups within a larger index or portfolio.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Correct weighting logic and handling firms with multiple sub-sectors.
assembly_hints: Often used after metric computation skills.

entries.canonical_name: Compile company profiles for private targets
entries.business_meaning: Ability to research and synthesize key information (description, valuation, funding, investors, customers) for private companies in a sector.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Finding reliable private company data; non-standard formats.
assembly_hints: Often combined with comparable company analysis.

entries.canonical_name: Perform comparable company analysis on Revenue, EBITDA, PE multiples
entries.business_meaning: Ability to identify a set of public comparables and compute valuation multiples (Revenue, EBITDA, PE) for benchmarking.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Selecting appropriate peers and normalizing financial metrics across companies.
assembly_hints: Often requires financial data retrieval and normalization first.

entries.canonical_name: Structure financial analysis into presentation slides
entries.business_meaning: Ability to synthesize financial research into executive-ready slide decks with clear narratives and visuals.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Balancing comprehensiveness with conciseness for senior audiences.
assembly_hints: Often combines multiple analysis skills into a single deliverable.

entries.canonical_name: Summarize macroeconomic environment for a target region
entries.business_meaning: Ability to gather and summarize key macro indicators (GDP, inflation, demographics, etc.) for a given region to inform strategy.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Selecting relevant indicators and providing balanced analysis.
assembly_hints: Often used to set context for industry or company-specific analysis.

entries.canonical_name: Analyze venture capital and technology market landscape in a region
entries.business_meaning: Ability to research and summarize the state of venture capital activity, technology startups, and investment trends in a region.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Finding reliable and comparable data across countries.
assembly_hints: Often paired with industry deep-dives like fintech.

entries.canonical_name: Evaluate fintech landscape for investment opportunities
entries.business_meaning: Ability to map the fintech ecosystem in a region, including key subsectors, players, regulatory environment, and potential synergies.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Rapidly changing regulatory and competitive landscape.
assembly_hints: Often requires macro and venture market context first.

entries.canonical_name: Implement multiple numerical pricing methods for American options
entries.business_meaning: Ability to develop and code multiple numerical approaches (binomial trees, finite differences, Monte Carlo) for pricing American options.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Handling early exercise feature and ensuring convergence.
assembly_hints: Often used for comparative analysis of methodologies.

entries.canonical_name: Benchmark computational performance of pricing algorithms
entries.business_meaning: Ability to measure and compare runtime and accuracy of different numerical methods to guide production deployment.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Accounting for variance in Monte Carlo and ensuring fair comparisons.
assembly_hints: Typically used after implementing multiple methods.

entries.canonical_name: Generate convergence and pricing comparison visualizations
entries.business_meaning: Ability to create visualizations that illustrate convergence behavior, pricing differences, and runtime benchmarks for quantitative analysis.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Choosing informative plot types and axes for clarity.
assembly_hints: Often combined with benchmarking skills.

entries.canonical_name: Analyze commodity market fundamentals (oil and gas)
entries.business_meaning: Ability to analyze supply-demand dynamics, geopolitical impacts, and price drivers for oil and natural gas markets.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Integrating multiple data sources and geopolitical analysis.
assembly_hints: Often used to support trading strategy development.

entries.canonical_name: Design portfolio optimization under constraints
entries.business_meaning: Ability to allocate assets within defined constraints (sector limits, duration, etc.) to maximize returns over a horizon.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Handling multiple constraints and non-linear objectives.
assembly_hints: Requires market analysis as input.

entries.canonical_name: Propose trading and sales strategy based on market analysis
entries.business_meaning: Ability to formulate a concrete set of trading and sales actions derived from fundamental market analysis and portfolio objectives.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Balancing conviction with risk management and regulatory compliance.
assembly_hints: Often follows market analysis and portfolio optimization skills.

entries.canonical_name: Construct Risk Assessment Questions for Grant Applicant Financial Management and Internal Controls
entries.business_meaning: Design a structured set of questions to evaluate a grant applicant's financial management and internal control systems, applicable across different applicant types.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Must cover diverse applicant types (universities, non-profits, local governments) while ensuring all relevant risk areas are addressed without being overly prescriptive.
failure_modes: Inconsistent coverage of financial and internal control aspects
Questions not aligned with regulatory requirements (2 C.F.R. 200.205)
Questions too vague to elicit meaningful risk insights
assembly_hints: Combine with data extraction skills to auto-populate from applicant records
Use alongside scoring rubric generation for risk classification

entries.canonical_name: Map Statutory Requirements to Binary Compliance Test Questions
entries.business_meaning: Convert specific legal provisions into closed-ended (Yes/No/Not Applicable) test questions to verify compliance during audits.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Must interpret legal text precisely and phrase questions to avoid ambiguity while covering all critical elements of the statute.
failure_modes: Incorrectly limiting answers to Yes/No/NA when more nuance is needed
Missing edge cases not explicitly covered by statute
assembly_hints: Can be chained with exception statement generation to automate audit documentation
Works with skill that parses statutes into logical elements

entries.canonical_name: Write Exception Statements for Regulatory Non-Compliance Findings
entries.business_meaning: Craft a narrative that explains how a specific failure to comply with a regulatory requirement occurred, suitable for audit reporting.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Must mirror regulatory tone and clearly articulate the gap between required action and actual behavior, often requiring interpretation of handbook language.
failure_modes: Missing specific details about the failure mode
Statement too generic, not linking to specific regulatory text
Tone too legalistic or too soft
assembly_hints: Combines with compliance test question generation to fully automate audit workpapers
May require input from data analysis skills that identify non-compliance events

entries.canonical_name: Compute Expenditure-to-Time Elapsed Ratio for Grant Spending Analysis
entries.business_meaning: Calculate the percentage of grant funds spent relative to the percentage of the project period elapsed, to identify spending rate anomalies.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires accurate date math and handling of partial periods; straightforward calculation.
failure_modes: Incorrect date difference calculation (e.g., using calendar vs business days)
Not handling zero elapsed time edge case
assembly_hints: Can be used as input to more complex risk scoring models
Combine with threshold-based flagging skill to identify fast/slow spenders

entries.canonical_name: Identify Fast- and Slow-Spending Patterns as Compliance Risk Indicators
entries.business_meaning: Apply predefined thresholds to spending ratios to flag grants that may indicate non-compliance risk due to anomalously fast or slow spending.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Thresholds are arbitrary; need to consider context (e.g., project type) and avoid false positives.
failure_modes: Flagging grants with legitimate front-loaded spending
Missing slow spenders due to incorrect threshold
Not documenting rationale for threshold application
assembly_hints: Can feed into risk scoring or workflow for further investigation
Depends on spending ratio skill

entries.canonical_name: Analyze Transaction Networks for Money Laundering Connections
entries.business_meaning: Trace and correlate transactions between linked entities (individuals, businesses) to uncover patterns indicative of money laundering, such as layering or structuring.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires synthesizing diverse data types (account statements, beneficial ownership, transaction history) and identifying non-obvious links.
failure_modes: Failing to document the logical chain of evidence
Misinterpreting legitimate business transactions as suspicious
assembly_hints: May integrate with regulatory threshold detection skill
Often precedes SAR writing skill

entries.canonical_name: Correlate Beneficial Ownership with Transaction Activity
entries.business_meaning: Cross-reference business ownership data with transaction history to identify discrepancies or suspicious patterns (e.g., personal expenses through business accounts).
entries.hidden_difficulty: Ownership structures may be complex, and transactions can be mislabeled. Requires careful integration of two data sources.
failure_modes: False positives due to legitimate personal/business mingling
assembly_hints: Can trigger further transaction review skills
Often part of a larger AML investigation workflow

entries.canonical_name: Reconcile Audit Evidence from Multiple Sources
entries.business_meaning: Reconcile audit evidence obtained from different sources (e.g., inspection, observation, reperformance) to ensure consistency and completeness.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires understanding of different evidence types and their reliability to identify and resolve inconsistencies.
assembly_hints: Combine with evidence reliability evaluation skill
Use when audit evidence came from multiple procedures

entries.canonical_name: Evaluate Reliability of Audit Evidence
entries.business_meaning: Assess the reliability of audit evidence based on source, nature, and circumstances, as required by auditing standards.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires professional judgment and understanding of factors affecting reliability such as independence, objectivity, and corroboration.
assembly_hints: Combines with control testing to determine appropriate audit procedures
Precedes evidence reconciliation

entries.canonical_name: Apply Sampling in Tests of Controls
entries.business_meaning: Design and implement sampling techniques to test internal controls, including selection, execution, and evaluation of results.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires understanding of sampling risk, statistical vs. non-statistical sampling, and implications for control reliability.
assembly_hints: May be combined with reliability evaluation to assess control effectiveness
Often precedes exception handling and evidence reconciliation

entries.canonical_name: Handle Exceptions in Control Testing
entries.business_meaning: Identify, document, and evaluate exceptions found during tests of controls to determine their impact on control effectiveness and audit strategy.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires judgment to distinguish between isolated incidents and systemic control failures, and to assess materiality.
assembly_hints: Feeds into overall audit evidence evaluation and reporting
Follows sample testing

entries.canonical_name: Corroborate Audit Evidence from Different Procedures
entries.business_meaning: Corroborate audit evidence obtained from different procedures to increase confidence and support conclusions.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires understanding of how different procedures complement each other and ability to identify contradictory evidence.
failure_modes: Insufficient corroboration leading to weak audit conclusions
assembly_hints: Increases overall audit evidence quality
Works alongside evidence reconciliation and reliability evaluation

entries.canonical_name: Validate audit evidence sufficiency and appropriateness
entries.business_meaning: Evaluates whether collected audit evidence is sufficient and appropriate to support audit conclusions, based on authoritative standards.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires subjective judgment about the relevance and reliability of different evidence types, balancing professional skepticism with efficiency.
failure_modes: Misjudging reliability of evidence from non-independent sources
assembly_hints: Combine with risk assessment skills to tailor evidence sufficiency thresholds
Use after evidence collection to confirm completeness

entries.canonical_name: Document audit procedures and rationale
entries.business_meaning: Captures the procedures performed, results, and rationale in audit workpapers to meet documentation standards and support conclusions.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Must reflect the full scope of work without oversimplification; requires clear linkage between risk, procedure, and evidence.
assembly_hints: Pair with evidence validation skill to document which evidence was deemed sufficient
Standardize documentation templates for consistency

entries.canonical_name: Reperform reconciliation calculations
entries.business_meaning: Independently recalculates figures in a reconciliation to verify mathematical accuracy and detect errors.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires careful attention to detail and understanding of the reconciliation formula (e.g., book balance to bank balance).
failure_modes: Assuming prior period figures are correct
assembly_hints: Combine with trace skill to support recalculation with source documentation
Use as an input to evidence sufficiency assessment

entries.canonical_name: Trace reconciling items to supporting documents
entries.business_meaning: Follows each reconciling item (e.g., outstanding checks, deposits in transit) back to original source documents to verify existence and accuracy.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Some items may lack clear external evidence; requires judgment on alternative procedures (e.g., cutoff tests).
failure_modes: Accepting internal documents as sole evidence
Missing stale items that should be investigated
assembly_hints: Pairs with investigation skill for unresolved items
Used after reperformance to confirm items are real

entries.canonical_name: Investigate reconciling items for exceptions
entries.business_meaning: Analyzes reconciling items that are unusual, aged, or unexplained to determine root cause and appropriate disposition (e.g., adjustment, disclosure).
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires understanding of business context, potential fraud indicators, and regulatory requirements for reporting.
failure_modes: Dismissing large or old items as timing differences without evidence
assembly_hints: Coordinate with fraud detection skills if indicators arise
Follow after trace skill to identify items needing investigation

entries.canonical_name: Assess Material Weakness in Internal Control
entries.business_meaning: Reusable capability to evaluate whether a control deficiency or combination of deficiencies constitutes a material weakness in internal control over financial reporting, based on audit evidence.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires professional judgment to aggregate deficiencies and consider compensating controls; involves probabilistic reasoning about likelihood and magnitude of misstatement.
assembly_hints: Combine with control testing results
Integrate with financial statement audit findings
Reference PCAOB AS5 guidance for definition of material weakness

entries.canonical_name: Test Operating Effectiveness of Internal Controls
entries.business_meaning: Capability to perform tests of controls to determine whether they are operating as designed throughout the period, including inquiry, observation, inspection, and reperformance.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires designing tests that cover all relevant attributes and timing; sampling risk and reliance on evidence from multiple periods add complexity.
assembly_hints: Combine with design evaluation
Consider entity-level controls impact
Use PCAOB AS5 guidance on nature, timing, and extent of tests

entries.canonical_name: Evaluate Control Deficiencies and Classify Severity
entries.business_meaning: Reusable skill to assess the severity of a control deficiency (deficiency, significant deficiency, material weakness) considering the likelihood and magnitude of potential misstatement.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires qualitative and quantitative judgment; need to consider aggregation of multiple deficiencies and existence of mitigating controls.
assembly_hints: Consider PCAOB AS5 material weakness definition
Reference KPMG ICFR Handbook guidance on deficiency evaluation
Use COSO framework for control criteria

entries.canonical_name: Apply COSO Components to Evaluate Control Environment
entries.business_meaning: Capability to use the COSO Internal Control-Integrated Framework (five components: control environment, risk assessment, control activities, information & communication, monitoring) to evaluate the effectiveness of an entity's internal control system.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires understanding of how components interrelate and how to map entity-level controls to COSO principles; subjective assessment of tone at the top.
assembly_hints: Link to financial reporting objectives
Start with control environment as foundation
Use COSO principles for each component

entries.canonical_name: Select Controls for Testing Based on Risk Assessment
entries.business_meaning: Reusable capability to prioritize and select controls for testing based on the risk of material misstatement, considering control design, complexity, and reliance on automated vs. manual controls.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires balancing coverage and efficiency; judgment on whether to test entity-level controls vs. process-level controls; integration with financial statement audit risk assessment.
assembly_hints: Align with PCAOB AS5 requirements
Consider COSO risk assessment component
Use KPMG ICFR Handbook guidance on risk-based approaches

entries.canonical_name: Document Control Testing Procedures and Results
entries.business_meaning: Reusable skill to prepare clear, complete, and compliant documentation of control testing procedures, evidence obtained, conclusions reached, and any identified deficiencies, supporting the audit opinion.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires understanding of auditing standards for documentation (e.g., PCAOB AS1215); ensuring sufficiency and objectivity of evidence; integrating with prior year workpapers.
failure_modes: Lack of clarity on procedures performed
assembly_hints: Ensure cross-referencing to risk assessment
Reference PCAOB AS5 and AS1215 documentation requirements
Use KPMG handbook examples as templates

entries.canonical_name: Verify audit documentation completeness and clarity
entries.business_meaning: Evaluates whether audit documentation is sufficiently detailed to enable an experienced auditor to understand the procedures, results, and conclusions.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires applying professional judgment to determine sufficiency of documentation, as standards are principles-based.
failure_modes: Overlooking missing documentation for significant matters
assembly_hints: Combine with 'Assess sufficiency of audit evidence' for comprehensive review
Use as a quality control step before final report issuance

entries.canonical_name: Assess control design and operating effectiveness
entries.business_meaning: Evaluates whether a control is designed appropriately to mitigate risks and whether it has operated effectively over time based on test evidence.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires understanding of control objectives and ability to correlate test results with design intent; may involve sampling and professional judgment.
assembly_hints: Can be integrated with risk assessment tasks
Precedes remediation planning if deficiencies found

entries.canonical_name: Scope internal controls for compliance
entries.business_meaning: Identifies which controls are relevant to compliance objectives based on financial statements and business processes, considering risk and materiality.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires understanding of entity-level controls, process flows, and risk assessment to determine which controls are in scope.
failure_modes: Omitting key controls due to incomplete process understanding
Scoping too broadly leading to inefficiency
assembly_hints: Feeds into control documentation and testing
Should align with materiality thresholds

entries.canonical_name: Validate control ownership assignment
entries.business_meaning: Confirms that each control has an assigned owner responsible for its operation and documentation, as required for compliance.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires checking documentation against organizational structures; ownership may be ambiguous or outdated.
assembly_hints: Combine with control documentation update
Facilitates remediation accountability

entries.canonical_name: Identify and document remediation plans for control gaps
entries.business_meaning: Develops a plan to address control deficiencies, including corrective actions, responsible parties, and timelines.
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires prioritization of deficiencies and coordination with control owners; plans must be realistic and tracked.
assembly_hints: Follows control deficiency identification
Input to ongoing monitoring

entries.canonical_name: Assess alignment of control objectives with financial statement assertions
entries.business_meaning: Determines whether control objectives properly address the relevant financial statement assertions (e.g., existence, completeness, valuation).
entries.hidden_difficulty: Requires understanding of the link between controls and assertions; may involve mapping and testing for coverage gaps.
failure_modes: Failing to update alignment when assertions change
assembly_hints: Baseline for designing test procedures
Combines with risk assessment to prioritize controls
